selection_reasoning: These four tasks form a coherent exploration-and-mining sequence. The agent must first locate colored glass structures (yellow stained glass and brown stained glass pane) which serve as landmarks/waypoints in the scene. The brown stained glass pane area leads to the light gray stained glass pane that must be mined. The yellow stained glass area leads to the dead horn coral block that must be mined. This creates two parallel branches: finding a visual landmark → mining a nearby target block. The 'find' tasks require navigation and visual identification, while the 'mine' tasks require the agent to break specific blocks. The find tasks must precede mining because the landmarks guide the agent to the correct locations where the mineable blocks are placed.
